Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be a [quantum universe](#def:quantum-universe) over the commutative ring $R$.

**Definition.** The **:defterm[Grothendieck group]{#grothendieck-group}** $K_0(\mathbf{C})$ is the abelian group generated by the isomorphism classes $[X]$ of objects of $\mathbf{C}$, subject to the relations $[X \oplus Y] = [X] + [Y]$. (This is the *split* Grothendieck group, appropriate to an additive category with no exact structure imposed; on any split-semisimple subcategory every short exact sequence splits and the split and exact Grothendieck groups coincide.)

**The block presentation on a split-semisimple slice.** Whenever an endomorphism algebra or full subcategory splits into a finite set $\widehat{A}$ of orthogonal blocks with simple objects $V_\lambda$ ($\lambda \in \widehat{A}$) such that every object in the slice is a finite direct sum of the $V_\lambda$ ([simple objects](#rem:simple-objects-V)), the Grothendieck group of that slice is the free abelian group on the blocks:

$$
  K_0(\mathbf{C}) \;=\; \bigoplus_{\lambda \in \widehat{A}} \mathbb{Z}\,[V_\lambda] \;\cong\; \mathbb{Z}^{\widehat{A}}.
$$

Two homomorphisms out of $K_0(\mathbf{C})$ are used throughout the monograph. The *rank* $K_0(\mathbf{C}) \to \mathbb{Z}$ sends each simple class $[V_\lambda]$ to $1$, counting simple constituents. In any [rigid monoidal category](#def:rigid-monoidal-category), the categorical trace dimension $\dim_{\mathbf{C}}(X) = \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_X) \in \operatorname{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbf{1}) \cong R$ is additive under direct sums and therefore extends to a group homomorphism

$$
  \dim_{\mathbf{C}} \colon K_0(\mathbf{C}) \longrightarrow R, \qquad \sum_\lambda n_\lambda [V_\lambda] \longmapsto \sum_\lambda n_\lambda \dim_{\mathbf{C}}(V_\lambda).
$$

**The ring structure.** The tensor product of $\mathbf{C}$ descends to $K_0(\mathbf{C})$ via $[X]\cdot[Y] = [X \otimes Y]$ because $\otimes$ distributes over $\oplus$; when $\mathbf{C}$ is braided, the braiding makes $K_0(\mathbf{C})$ a commutative ring — the *representation ring* (or *fusion ring*) of $\mathbf{C}$ — with unit $[\mathbf{1}]$. The categorical trace dimension is a ring homomorphism, since $\mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_{X \otimes Y}) = \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_X)\,\mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_Y)$ in any rigid braided monoidal category \cite{kassel1995}.

**The prototype example.** For $\mathbf{C} = \mathrm{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}(2))$, with simple objects $V_n$ of dimension $n + 1$, the Clebsch--Gordan rule $V_1 \otimes V_n \cong V_{n-1} \oplus V_{n+1}$ identifies $K_0(\mathbf{C})$ with the polynomial ring $\mathbb{Z}[x]$ generated by $x = [V_1]$: each $[V_n]$ is the Chebyshev polynomial in $x$ determined recursively by $x\,[V_n] = [V_{n-1}] + [V_{n+1}]$, with rank $1$ and classical dimension $n + 1$. Under deformation of the braided category, the simple classes $[V_n]$ and their Clebsch--Gordan multiplication law in $K_0$ remain unchanged; what deforms is the trace evaluation homomorphism $K_0(\mathbf{C}) \to R$ \cite{bghl-2017}.
